subject: Career
title: Reciprocity: The Give-to-Get Principle
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Reciprocity: The Give-to-Get Principle.

hook.text: The recruiter gives you extra PTO. Now you feel obligated to accept the lower base. That's reciprocity.

buildup.text: Reciprocity is a deep social instinct: when someone gives, we feel compelled to give back.

discovery.text: In negotiation, small concessions from the employer create pressure to concede on bigger items.

twist.text: You can use it too: 'I'm flexible on start date if we can meet on compensation.'

climax.text: Strategic concessions on low-priority items buy goodwill for high-priority ones.

punchline.text: Give what costs you little. Get what matters most.

quiz.question: How does reciprocity affect salary negotiation?
options: Small concessions create pressure to concede on bigger items

details.summary: The reciprocity principle states that people feel compelled to return favors. In salary negotiation, offering flexibility on start date, work arrangement, or travel can trigger reciprocity from the employer, making them more willing to improve financial terms in return.
details.whyItMatters: Negotiation is most effective when both sides feel they are gaining. Strategic concessions on lower-priority items often unlock higher-priority financial outcomes.
takeaways: Offering concessions triggers the employer's reciprocity instinct
Choose low-cost concessions that carry high perceived value
Reciprocity works best when concessions feel voluntary and genuine

faq.question: What are examples of low-cost concessions I can offer?
faq.answer: Starting a week earlier, accepting a slightly different title, agreeing to an extra travel day per month, or volunteering for an onboarding project are all concessions that cost you little but signal flexibility and goodwill to the employer.

faq.question: Can reciprocity backfire in a salary negotiation?
faq.answer: If concessions appear calculated or manipulative, they can erode trust. The key is to offer genuinely helpful flexibility rather than fabricated sacrifices. Authenticity in concessions strengthens the relationship and the negotiation outcome.
